newsitem.title: USA: New Los Angeles police chief sworn in.
newsitem.headline: New Los Angeles police chief sworn in.

text.p: Bernard Parks was sworn in as Los Angeles' new police chief Tuesday, becoming the first black officer to rise from cop on the beat to top cop in America's second-largest city.
Parks' swearing-in came after the city council unanimously approved his nomination by Mayor Richard Riordan with a 12-0 vote.

The 32-year veteran of the force was handpicked by Riordan to take over a department whose image has been badly tarnished by accusations of racism and brutality following the 1991 videotaped beating of black motorist Rodney King by white officers.
Riordan has strongly denied he picked a black officer to lead the department in order to foster better relations between police and the city's large African American community.
"I am angry to think that people would think of Bernie Parks as a black chief. He is the chief of the LAPD, not the black half of the LAPD," Riordan said in a recent interview.
After being sworn in, Parks told the council, "I pledge to you that you have not made a bad decision and that you will be very pleased with the results."
Parks promised a major crackdown on crime, starting with the city's notorious street gangs, after being named by Riordan last month.

Known as a strict disciplinarian, the new chief also promised major reforms within the department. As part of those reforms all officers, no matter what their rank, would be held fully accountable for their actions, he said.

Parks replaces Willie Williams, whose five-year contract was not renewed earlier this year. Williams, who was the city's first black police chief, had been brought in to heal the wounds the LAPD suffered following King's beating.

But Williams, who came from Philadelphia, never gained the confidence of officers on the street and was accused by city council members of acting unethically by accepting hospitality and free hotel rooms from Las Vegas casinos.
